faq.q: What is the fastest HIPAA starting point for a Santa Ana clinic?
faq.a: Start with a current risk analysis, a vendor/BAA inventory, workforce training records, and documented rules for patient messaging, referrals, billing follow-up, and records requests.

faq.q: Does California replace HIPAA for Santa Ana clinics?
faq.a: No. HIPAA remains the federal baseline for covered entities and business associates. Santa Ana clinics should check current California materials before changing workflows because state oversight, medical-record, privacy, or incident expectations can change.

faq.q: Which vendors should a Santa Ana clinic review first?
faq.a: Review vendors that touch PHI first, especially messaging, forms, interpreter, scheduling, billing, and referral vendors. Confirm the workflow is allowed, the right plan or contract is in place, and a BAA is signed before PHI use.

faq.q: How often should a Santa Ana clinic review HIPAA evidence?
faq.a: Review high-change workflows monthly, run a broader evidence review quarterly, and refresh policies and training at least annually. Add extra reviews after vendor, staffing, location, or patient communication changes.
